부럽다.ex: 제 친구는 영어를 잘해서 정말 부러워요.
부럽다.x: My friend speaks English well, so I'm really jealous.
부럽다.e: Add -어하다 to describe someone else's envy: 친구가 저를 부러워해요.
부럽다.t: 부러워요! is a friendly 'I'm so jealous!'; bitter or romantic jealousy is 질투하다.

계획하다.ex: 우리는 다음 달 여행을 같이 계획하고 있어요.
계획하다.x: We're planning next month's trip together.
계획하다.t: With the noun, say 계획을 세우다 'to make a plan' — literally 'to stand up a plan.'

계속하다.x: Even if it's hard, I'm going to keep exercising.
계속하다.e: Two syllables that both mean 'carry on' — doubled for emphasis.
계속하다.t: 계속 alone works as an adverb: 계속 비가 와요 = It keeps raining. Pronounced [계소카다].

노력.x: You need effort to get good results.
노력.e: Literally 'striving strength' — putting your power into it.

상관없다.m: to not matter, to be unrelated; to not care
상관없다.x: Any food at all is fine with me.
상관없다.t: Pronounced [상과넙따]. Handy reply when asked your preference: 저는 상관없어요.

예정.ex: 저는 다음 주에 부산에 갈 예정이에요.
예정.x: I'm planning to go to Busan next week.
예정.t: Use the pattern -(으)ㄹ 예정이에요 to say something is scheduled or planned.

회복하다.x: After getting plenty of rest, I recovered my health.
회복하다.t: It works beyond health too: 신뢰를 회복하다, 'to regain trust.'

존경하다.m: to respect, to look up to, to admire
존경하다.ex: 제가 가장 존경하는 사람은 우리 어머니예요.
존경하다.x: The person I respect most is my mother.
존경하다.t: 존경하다 means looking up to someone; 존중하다 means respecting anyone's rights, opinions or choices.

주장하다.m: to claim, to argue, to insist
주장하다.x: He kept insisting that he was right.
주장하다.t: Usually used with -다고: 옳다고 주장하다 'to insist that one is right'.

선택.x: Which path you take is your choice.

발명하다.x: Edison invented many things during his life.

서명하다.x: Please write your name here and sign.
서명하다.t: In speech, 사인하다 is very common; 서명하다 sounds more official.

발령.x: I was assigned to the Busan branch.
발령.e: Literally 'issuing an order' — the company's order placing you in a post.
발령.t: Common patterns: 발령을 받다 (to be assigned) and 발령이 나다 (an assignment is made).

신입 사원.ex: 올해 우리 팀에 신입 사원이 두 명 들어왔어요.
신입 사원.x: Two new employees joined our team this year.
신입 사원.t: Often shortened to just 신입: 신입이 들어왔어요.

휴직.ex: 그녀는 건강 때문에 1년 동안 휴직을 했어요.
휴직.x: She took a one-year leave of absence for health reasons.
휴직.e: Literally 'resting from the job' — you keep the position while away.
휴직.t: 휴직 is a long leave where you keep your job; 휴가 is a short vacation.

대립.ex: 두 정당의 대립이 점점 심해지고 있습니다.
대립.x: The confrontation between the two parties is getting worse.
대립.t: 대립 is about opposing positions or sides; 갈등 is broader tension, emotional or social.

미성년자.ex: 미성년자는 술과 담배를 살 수 없습니다.
미성년자.x: Minors cannot buy alcohol or cigarettes.
미성년자.e: Literally 'person who has not yet completed their years'.
미성년자.t: In Korea, people under 19 count as 미성년자 for alcohol and tobacco.

중학생.x: I learned English for the first time when I was in middle school.

절정.x: The story reaches its climax in the last scene.
절정.t: Common pattern: 절정에 이르다 'reach a peak'; also for seasons, like 단풍이 절정이에요 'fall colors are at their peak'.

불법.x: Parking your car here is illegal.
불법.t: Common compounds: 불법 주차 'illegal parking', 불법 다운로드 'illegal downloading'.

계약금.ex: 집을 계약할 때 계약금으로 천만 원을 냈어요.
계약금.x: When I signed for the house, I paid ten million won as a down payment.
계약금.e: -금 = money for a purpose: 계약금, 보상금, 장학금.

기가 막히다.m: to be dumbfounded, to be speechless; to be amazing, to be incredible
기가 막히다.ex: 이 집 김치찌개는 정말 기가 막혀요.
기가 막히다.x: The kimchi stew at this place is absolutely amazing.
기가 막히다.e: Literally 'one's energy is blocked' — so shocked you can't breathe.
기가 막히다.t: Context decides the sense: shock at something bad, or praise for something amazingly good, like food.

온통.forms: 온통 + noun/state: 온통 하얗다, 머릿속이 온통 ~ 생각
온통.x: When I woke up in the morning, the whole world was white.
온통.e: Probably related to 온 'whole, entire', as in 온 세상.
온통.t: 머릿속이 온통 ~ 생각뿐이에요 means 'I can think of nothing but ~'.

개입하다.m: to intervene, to get involved, to interfere
개입하다.ex: 다른 사람의 부부 싸움에 개입하지 않는 게 좋아요.
개입하다.x: It's better not to get involved in other couples' fights.
개입하다.t: Pronounced [개이파다]; common in news about governments: 정부가 시장에 개입하다.

뒤집다.m: to turn over, to flip; to turn inside out; to overturn (a decision)
뒤집다.ex: 고기가 익으면 한 번 뒤집어 주세요.
뒤집다.x: When the meat is cooked, flip it once.

미숙하다.x: I'm still inexperienced at driving, so I'm being careful.

문맥.ex: 모르는 단어는 문맥을 보고 뜻을 추측해 보세요.
문맥.x: For unknown words, try guessing the meaning from the context.
문맥.t: 문맥 is context within a text; 맥락 is broader, including situations and history.

본능.x: A mother protecting her baby is instinct.
본능.e: Literally 'original ability': what you can do without learning.

면적.x: This park covers a very large area.

손에 익다.forms: 손에 익었어요 · 손에 익으면 · 손에 익은 일
손에 익다.m: to get the hang of something, to become practiced at it (lit. it ripens in the hand)
손에 익다.ex: 처음엔 어려웠는데 이제 일이 좀 손에 익었어요.
손에 익다.x: It was hard at first, but now I've got the hang of the work.
손에 익다.e: 익다 means 'to ripen' and also 'to become familiar'; the task becomes familiar to your hands.
손에 익다.t: Pronounced [소네 익따]. The task is the subject: 일이 손에 익다, not 제가 손에 익다.

정당방위.x: The court recognized his actions as self-defense.

중립성.x: The media must maintain political neutrality.
중립성.e: Literally 'the quality of standing in the middle'.
중립성.t: Pronounced [중닙썽] — nasalization plus a tense ㅆ.

선망.ex: 그 회사는 취업 준비생들의 선망의 대상이에요.
선망.x: That company is the envy of job seekers.
선망.t: Typical phrase: 선망의 대상 'object of envy' — admiring, not hostile.

미덥다.ex: 신입 사원이라서 아직은 좀 미덥지 않아요.
미덥다.x: He's a new employee, so he doesn't seem quite reliable yet.
미덥다.e: Built on 믿다 'to believe, trust' — think 'believable'.
미덥다.t: Most often used in the negative: 미덥지 않다 or 미덥지 못하다 'not quite trustworthy'.

과유불급.m: too much is as bad as too little; moderation is best
과유불급.x: Even exercise can be overdone, so don't push yourself too hard.
과유불급.e: Literally 'going too far is like falling short'; a saying attributed to Confucius.

발 벗고 나서다.forms: 발 벗고 나서요 · 발 벗고 나섰어요 · 발 벗고 나서서 돕다
발 벗고 나서다.m: to jump in wholeheartedly to help; to roll up one's sleeves
발 벗고 나서다.ex: 마을 사람들이 발 벗고 나서서 청소를 도왔어요.
발 벗고 나서다.x: The villagers rolled up their sleeves and helped with the cleanup.
발 벗고 나서다.e: Literally 'to take off one's shoes and step forward,' ready for hard work.

유생.ex: 조선 시대 유생들은 서원에서 학문을 닦았습니다.
유생.x: Confucian scholars in the Joseon era pursued their studies at seowon academies.

규격화.ex: 부품을 규격화하면 생산 비용을 줄일 수 있습니다.
규격화.x: Standardizing parts can reduce production costs.
규격화.t: Pronounced [규겨콰]; 규격화되다 is the passive 'to be standardized'.

심박수.x: Your heart rate goes up when you exercise.

묘책.ex: 아무리 생각해도 뾰족한 묘책이 떠오르지 않아요.
묘책.x: No matter how hard I think, no clever solution comes to mind.
묘책.e: Literally 'clever plan'; -책 = plan or measure: 대책, 해결책.

침공.ex: 러시아의 우크라이나 침공으로 많은 난민이 발생했습니다.
침공.x: Russia's invasion of Ukraine created many refugees.
침공.t: 침공 is a military invasion; 침략 stresses the aggression behind it.

전쟁범죄.x: The international community defined attacks on civilians as war crimes.

교섭.ex: 양국 정부는 포로 송환 문제를 놓고 교섭을 벌였습니다.
교섭.x: The two governments negotiated over the repatriation of prisoners.
교섭.t: 교섭 sounds more formal than 협상; labor talks are 단체교섭.

폭식증.x: My binge eating gets worse when I'm stressed.

탄성.ex: 고무줄은 탄성이 좋아서 늘어났다가 다시 돌아와요.
탄성.x: A rubber band is very elastic, so it stretches and then snaps back.
탄성.e: Literally 'bounce nature'. Homonym warning: 탄성 also means a gasp of admiration.

첨단산업.ex: 정부는 반도체 같은 첨단산업을 적극 지원하고 있습니다.
첨단산업.x: The government is actively supporting high-tech industries like semiconductors.
첨단산업.e: Literally 'pointed-tip industry' — at the very tip of progress.
첨단산업.t: 첨단 works as a prefix too: 첨단 장비 'state-of-the-art equipment.'

고증.m: historical research, verification by evidence; period accuracy
고증.ex: 이 사극은 시대 고증이 정확하기로 유명해요.
고증.x: This historical drama is famous for its accurate period detail.
고증.e: Literally 'examine and prove' — checking facts against old sources.
고증.t: Common in reviews: 고증이 잘 됐다 / 고증 오류 (historical inaccuracy) for dramas and films.

파란만장.m: full of ups and downs, eventful (life or history)
파란만장.x: My grandmother lived a life full of ups and downs.
파란만장.e: Literally 'billows ten thousand jang high' (a jang is about ten feet) — a life tossed by enormous waves.
파란만장.t: Almost always appears as 파란만장한 삶, 인생, or 역사.

희박하다.x: At the mountaintop the air is thin, so it's hard to breathe.
희박하다.t: Classic collocation: 가능성이 희박하다 'the chances are slim'.

연대의식.ex: 같은 어려움을 겪으면서 노동자들 사이에 연대의식이 생겼어요.
연대의식.x: Going through the same hardship created a sense of solidarity among the workers.
연대의식.e: Literally 'linked-belt awareness': people bound together by a shared cause.

절충하다.m: to compromise, to strike a middle ground, to blend
절충하다.ex: 두 회사는 오랜 협상 끝에 가격을 절충했습니다.
절충하다.x: After long negotiations, the two companies settled on a compromise price.
절충하다.e: Literally 'break toward the middle' — meeting halfway between positions.
절충하다.t: 절충안 'compromise proposal' is the most frequent derivative.

영속성.x: Innovation is necessary for a company to last.

건곤일척.m: staking everything on one throw, an all-or-nothing gamble
건곤일척.ex: 두 팀은 결승전에서 건곤일척의 승부를 벌였습니다.
건곤일척.x: The two teams fought an all-or-nothing battle in the final.
건곤일척.e: Literally 'heaven and earth on one throw of the dice'.
